sources: Competitor audit 11/11/2026, content plan study 11/11/2026, inspo visual 11/11/2026, content style reference 02/11/2026, Merlin's Instagram read 15/11/2026

borrow.idea: Numbered steps in the caption for one pot, one dish (Meatballs Al Forno, 67K likes). Order link in the last line.
borrow.use: Lamb shank tease and process posts.

borrow.idea: Dish name plus components as the whole caption, one cosy mood line, no hard sell (1,338 likes on a pork chop reel).
borrow.use: Cooler weather mood posts for stews.

borrow.idea: A title card in the dish colour, then silence. Recipe highlights in the caption.
borrow.use: Name the dish posts for new items.

borrow.idea: A repeatable named series, so people know what the next one is (Trashy to Classy).
borrow.use: Hour by hour and Worth the wait as named series.

borrow.idea: Sharing post (228 likes, best of its latest 6) and a game post once a month. Footer repeats price and add on.
borrow.use: Share a pot with someone, and a pick a sauce poll.

borrow.idea: Warm playful voice, schedule post pinned, pre order rhythm that sets expectations.
borrow.use: Pinned post with the 2 day lead time for premium items.

borrow.idea: Exact grams and technique as authority (Bolognese Precanonica).
borrow.use: One technique post: why the sofritto takes 8 hours.

avoid.idea: 95 second face led reels. Needs a face on camera and hours of editing.

avoid.why: Production heavy, off brand for Merlin's calm tone.
Approximate with one warm side lamp instead.

avoid.idea: Posts with no price and no order path, and a capped 20 orders a day story.
avoid.why: Merlin's wins on a clear direct order line and casual prices.

avoid.idea: High energy volume and event posts.
avoid.why: Competes on Affordable Comfort at volume. Merlin's stays Premium Ingredients, comfortable price.

avoid.idea: Grab only calls to action and copy that compares to other platforms.
avoid.why: Merlin's sells direct plus Grab. Never attack or compare with Grab.

avoid.idea: Emoji only or tag only captions.
avoid.why: Merlin's best reel had a clear label and a clear promise.

style.visual: Warm, dark and glossy. Top down pot macros in steel pots, amber sauce, one side lamp. Best reel (6,981 views, median 222) was one unbroken 16 second macro with one text label. Gaps: most reels have no hook text, none end on a finished dish reveal.
style.context: Slow cooking as craft. The sofritto series (Hour 1, only 7 hours to go; aromatics merging; the trinity is complete) is a real series. Bio promise: Homemade flavours, done properly. Casual prices.
style.copy: Sensory hook, sharp invitation, standard footer. Warm, friendly and fun, led by appetite: make people hungry and make them smile. Short, punchy and a little cheeky, never quiet or flat. English only. Older captions end with DM or GrabFood link in bio, which is superseded by the order app link. Rules: slash prices only, no percentages.

proposals.title: The 8 hour sofritto, finished
proposals.visual: One continuous macro of the finished sauce in the pot, wooden spoon lift. Cover text "Worth the wait". Finish on the plated pasta with steam. Crop 4:5 for the grid cover.
proposals.caption: Eight hours. Onion, carrot and celery, melting into amber. This is the base of every sauce we make, and yes, it smells as good as it looks. Worth the wait.
proposals.why: Your best reel was one unbroken macro with one label (6,981 views). Repeating a proven format is the lowest risk first post, and the sauces behind it are your best sellers.
proposals.avoid: No cuts faster than every 3 seconds

proposals.title: Red Wine Beef Stew, cooler evenings
proposals.visual: Top down on the stew bowl, one side lamp, dark table. Dish name and components only on the cover.
proposals.caption: Cooler evenings called. Red Wine Beef Stew answered. Tender beef, red wine, carrot and a gravy that coats the spoon. Come hungry. Order 2 days ahead.
proposals.why: A cosy, appetite first post for the cooler weather. It names the dish and its parts with a smile, which earns trust before the next ask.
proposals.avoid: No hard sell, no price in the caption

proposals.title: Lamb shank, Hour 1 (tease)
proposals.hook: Hour 1. The shanks meet the pot.
proposals.visual: Top down on the pot. Cover text "Hour 1". Clip 1: shanks searing, deep brown. Clip 2: onion and garlic dropping in. End on the closed lid.
proposals.caption: Hour 1. The lamb shanks have met the pot and the kitchen already smells like a very good decision. Something slow and special is coming soon.
proposals.why: Starts the lamb story early and shows the craft that justifies the price. No order link yet, so nobody is sent to a dish they cannot buy.
proposals.avoid: No order link until the lamb can be ordered

proposals.title: This is how it arrives
proposals.visual: Reference: @rhoifood bowl held above the branded bag. A hand holds a bowl of Red Wine Beef Stew just above your closed bag, your sticker facing the camera. Dark, moody backdrop, one side lamp, the bag lower third, the bowl catching the light. Hand only, no face. Crop 4:5.
proposals.caption: Plot twist: this is what dinner looks like when it arrives. Red Wine Beef Stew, slow cooked for hours, packed up and on its way to your door.
proposals.why: People order food they cannot see, so showing the bag and the bowl answers "what will I get" before a first order. The sticker on every package builds familiarity. The look comes from your @rhoifood reference.
proposals.borrow: @rhoifood bowl above the bag, one sticker as the brand mark
proposals.avoid: No platform logos on the bag in the shot, no comparisons

proposals.title: Slow Braised Lamb Shank (reveal)
proposals.visual: One hero shot at 45 degrees, steam rising, shank on a dark plate with carrots and gravy. Title card in warm amber, then no other text. One spoon lift to finish. Post only once lamb can be ordered in the order app, and move the date to match.
proposals.caption: Meet the Slow Braised Lamb Shank. One shank, sweet carrots and 300g of gravy, braised for hours until it falls off the bone. Fork optional. Order 2 days ahead.
proposals.why: The payoff of the tease. A title card and one spoon lift keep it simple. The 2 day lead time is a true deadline that turns interest into orders.
proposals.borrow: @jose.kallioinen title card, @bshnuez dish name plus components
proposals.avoid: Do not post before the lamb can be ordered

proposals.title: A pot for dad (Father's Day, 05/12)
proposals.visual: Slide 1: a pot and two bowls. Slide 2: the pot being lifted. Slide 3: dish name with "serves 2". Warm lamp, dark table. Post 02/12 so the 2 day lead time works for the long weekend 05/12 to 07/12.
proposals.caption: Father's Day dinner, sorted. Red Wine Beef Stew, Tuscan Pork Braise or the new Slow Braised Lamb Shank, slow cooked for hours and delivered to your door. Dad just has to show up hungry. Order 2 days ahead.
proposals.why: Father's Day on 05/12 is a Thai holiday and a long weekend, so it speaks to the Thai audience. Posting on 02/12 respects the 2 day lead time.

proposals.title: Pick the sauce
proposals.visual: Two pots side by side from above. Story poll sticker added in the app. Reveal the winner in a Stories reply.
proposals.caption: Spicy Rosso or Noir Ragu? Tough choice, we know. Vote in Stories and the winner goes in the pot next.
proposals.why: Gets people to do something instead of just looking. A game post gave a competitor its best of the latest 6 (228 likes). Votes also tell you what people want. Keep it to one a month.
proposals.avoid: No more than one game post a month

proposals.title: Why we brown first
proposals.visual: Close on meat hitting the oil, then the dark crust lifting with water. Cover text "Brown first". Two clips of 4s, one reveal of 4s.
proposals.caption: Brown first. Always. That dark crust on the pan is where the flavour lives, so every bit goes back into the braise. We do not do shortcuts.
proposals.why: Shows technique, which supports the price, and it works for any dish. It also gives the lamb tease a few days to breathe before the reveal.
proposals.avoid: Share the idea, not the full recipe

proposals.title: Noir Ragu, the pot lift
proposals.visual: One continuous macro of Noir Ragu in the pot, a spoon lift, the sauce falling slowly. Cover text "Worth every hour". End on the plated pasta.
proposals.caption: Noir Ragu. Dark, deep and slow, and worth every hour. One spoon and you will understand.
proposals.why: A second payoff post, three weeks after the first, so the format builds familiarity without repeating the same dish. Noir Ragu is a top 3 seller.
proposals.avoid: Do not reuse the cp-11 shot

proposals.title: Christmas table, last orders 22/12
proposals.visual: Lamb shank or beef stew plated with rosemary and a candle, shot at 45 degrees. Cover text "Last orders 22/12". Confirm the last order date against your own capacity first.
proposals.caption: A slow pot for the Christmas table. Slow Braised Lamb Shank or Red Wine Beef Stew, cooked for hours so you can enjoy the day. Last orders 22/12, so please order 2 days ahead.
proposals.why: Christmas is the real European moment for Merlin's. A last orders date is a true deadline, so it gives people a reason to decide now.
proposals.avoid: Do not set a last order date you cannot meet

proposals.title: Open the bag
proposals.hook: Everything that comes in the bag.
proposals.visual: Reference: @rhoifood opened container with sauces in small pots and a tied spoon. Slide 1: the closed bag with your sticker. Slide 2: flat lay from above of exactly what comes in an order, container open, sides, spoon, anything you tuck in. Slide 3: close on the sticker or lid label. Warm grey or cream backdrop, hard side light. Shoot only what really goes in the bag.
proposals.caption: Open the bag. A slow cooked dish, everything that comes with it, and a little care on top. Unwrapping dinner is half the fun.
proposals.why: A second arrival post, after the first has been seen, shows the full order. A gift ready bag suits the Christmas run, and the layout (opened container, small pots, one tied detail) is straight from your @rhoifood reference.
proposals.avoid: Do not show anything that is not in a real order

story.headline: Six pillars, one job each. Two lamb posts, 6 days apart.

points.title: Why this mix
points.body: Every pillar comes from something that already worked for you or a competitor. Open Pillars to see the source.

points.title: Check before shooting
points.body: Post the lamb reveal only once lamb can be ordered. Confirm the Christmas last orders date (22/12).

pillars.job: Gets people to do something, and shows what they want.
pillars.from: @hangrybeefnoodle game posts. Votes are customer research and a community ritual. One a month.

pillars.name: How it arrives
pillars.job: Shows what the customer receives, so a first order feels safe and the brand is known before the box is opened.
pillars.from: Your @rhoifood reference: the bowl held above the branded bag on a dark backdrop, the labelled container with sauces in small pots and a tied spoon, one sticker on every package. Borrow the look, not the results (the reference posts have 5 to 6 likes). Also the Grab bag thank you card idea.
